findings.part: backchain_single_pass / quality_risk / carve-out exit clause (the printed `backchain-check` as part of the one-pass exit)
findings.claim: The exit clause 'the printed backchain-check passes on the repaired candidate' does not discriminate at the plan stage. The draft uses it to say the exit stays checkable and that a script check replaces the confirming review. That holds only for the step-plan loop, which 1.20.0 no longer offers as a whole loop.
findings.evidence: [M] I ran shiploop_backchain_graph.check, the packaged check behind `backchain-check`, on the 1.16.1 Luna plan-loop files under /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261003/v1161-battleship-luna/.shiploop-runs/work-20261003-225401-173a04/run/scratch/backchain-plan. generator-draft.json, elaborated-candidate.json and candidate-plan.json all return ok=True with 0 unconfirmed produces. elaborated-candidate.json is the pass-1 input: its sha256 prefix b66d62f0d55f equals candidate_identity in review-records/action-1-review.json. So the check passes before any pass runs, and it cannot see the three semantic defects pass 1 fixed (wrong supplier edge, unindexed API-concurrency obligation, omitted browser recovery report). Only the step-plan candidates (backchain-step-plan/review-records/review-0N-candidate-plan.json) fail, on invariant 4 (D1). [M] The check is record-only: the BACKCHAIN_CHECK comment in shiploop_prompts.py says 'nothing refuses a failing check', and the backchain-check help in shiploop_protocol.py says 'never gates'. So at plan the exit reduces to 'one cycle ran', judged by the model alone. [M] BACKCHAIN_NATIVE_CALLS offers a whole loop only at plan, and the audit stages offer only repair/revise after a finding.
findings.proposed_change: Say in the printed text, the carve-out and quality_risk that the exit is model-assessed and the check is a structural, record-only aid. Drop 'S-10 loop condition stays checkable' and drop D1 as evidence for the plan loop. Keep the check clause as a recorded receipt, not as a mitigation. State that the only later net for a plan-loop repair is the always-scheduled Improve child. Add the check receipt before and after pass 1 to the measurement section so the next run shows whether the check ever discriminates at plan.

findings.part: I3 (Backchain skill and docs: caller-selected gate) and its test
findings.claim: I3 omits skills/backchain/references/caller-contract.md. That file states the two-record rule unconditionally, so a host following it literally treats a one-pass completion as incomplete planning. The I3 test ('four documents') would not catch this. The 'caller packet' mechanism is also undefined.
findings.evidence: [M] caller-contract.md says 'Preserve access to both original qualifying review records ... a terminal receipt with only the latest review recoverable is incomplete planning'. convergence.md 'Terminal evidence and recovery' says either record unavailable 'leaves planning incomplete even when the exact runtime receipt says complete'. [M] The Backchain SKILL.md has several unconditional two-review statements: the frontmatter description, 'Source-aware native plan' step 4, and Procedure step 4 ('neither substitutes for the two consecutive planning reviews'). The draft names only 'description and the two-consecutive procedure line'. [M] The `backchain-caller/v1` packet in caller-contract.md is a closed JSON shape with no pass or gate field. 'A caller packet saying Backchain passes: one' therefore refers to the ShipLoop packet line, not to the v1 packet the host builds as caller-packet.json. [M] convergence.md defines qualifying reviews as those since the latest material reset 'plus that reset's record'. Under gate 0 with a non-trivial pass 1, only the reset record exists, so 'both' cannot be met unless the one-pass set is defined. [I] I2 lands before I3 in the draft, so the packet and the skill contradict between those commits. I2's route test does not read convergence.md.
findings.proposed_change: Add caller-contract.md to I3, and optionally the 'two consecutive' sentence in harness.md. Define the selection channel: either the ShipLoop packet line 'Backchain passes: one', or an optional `passes` field in the v1 packet. In both convergence.md and caller-contract.md, define the one-pass terminal evidence set (the single reset review record plus the check receipt). Make the I3 test scan all of skills/backchain for 'two consecutive' and 'both original qualifying', and require every hit to sit in a default/converge conditional. Land I3 together with I2, or have I2's route test also assert that convergence.md and caller-contract.md do not contradict the printed gate.

findings.part: spec_and_owner_rules: EXACT CARVE-OUT TEXT and I0
findings.claim: The carve-out wording is not sufficient as drafted. It names only S-10, although the draft's own adversarial evaluation says S-9 is weakened. 'No iteration cap is added' misdescribes a default exit that is a count of one. It omits the S-4/S-5/S-12 exception. The proposed I0 test would fail against the carve-out's own text. It does not supersede the existing owner-approved plan lines that say the two-pass exit stays.
findings.evidence: [M] done() in skills/improve/runtime/until-loop/scripts/until_loop_ephemeral.py completes when exit_assessment is satisfied and trivial_streak >= required_trivial_reviews. At gate 0 the second clause is vacuously true, so a single model report ends the loop. Today the runtime counts the two-review streak, and S-9 says completion is never 'the model's own judgment'. [M] SPEC.md S-10 says 'frozen contract the script writes and iterations the script counts', and the SPEC evidence table lists 'hand-built loop contracts' under model_glue for S-4/S-5. metrics.py GLUE_CONTRACT flags writes of `exit_condition|required_trivial_reviews`, so every Backchain-bearing run reports glue. [M] The drafted carve-out starts 'owner decision 2026-10-04', but the I0 test asserts 'Owner decision 2026-10-04'. A case-sensitive assert fails. Prefixing 'Except for the carve-out below,' also requires lower-casing 'There'. [M] SPEC 'Change admission' defines Anchor as the clause the change serves. This change weakens S-10 rather than serves it, so I0's 'anchor S-9/S-10' is mislabeled. The anchor is the owner request plus the run evidence. [M] docs/shiploop-backchain-validator-comparison-plan-2026-10-04.md Part C and I6 say 'The exit rule (two clean passes, no pass cap) is S-10 and stays unless SPEC S-10 is amended first', and B1 is 'every pass earns its time'. I0 supersedes neither. [I] The text attributes the decision to the owner on 2026-10-04 before D1 confirms the wording.
findings.proposed_change: Reword the carve-out. State that the default exit is one completed review/fix/check cycle, that completion is a single model-assessed report, that the numeric gate is 0, and that the loop continues with no numeric ceiling while a pass reports an open gap. Cite S-9 and S-10, and name the host-built contract as an accepted S-4/S-5/S-12 exception (a02). State that the check is structural and record-only. Fix the test strings, including case. Use the owner request and run evidence as the anchor. Land I0 only after D1 confirms the text. In I0, mark the comparison-plan lines (Part C, I6, B1) superseded with the date and reason, per the journal rule.

findings.part: backchain_single_pass: 'a conservative model costs 2 passes, not 7'; host-paraphrased contract
findings.claim: The 'about 2 passes' bound is an inference, not runtime-verified. Nothing in the design bounds the pass count except the model's own satisfied report, and the contract wording is left for the host to paraphrase.
findings.evidence: [M] I re-ran the vendored runtime in scratch. Gate 0 with non-trivial/satisfied completes after 1 action. Gate 0 with unsatisfied then satisfied completes at the second report. Unresolved plus satisfied is refused. A gate-0 report of unsatisfied or unknown continues, and a contract carrying max_iterations is refused, so there is no runtime ceiling. That verifies 'completes at the next satisfied report', not 'about 2 passes'. [M] The 1.16.1 start input (scratch/backchain-plan/until-loop-start-input.json) shows the host paraphrased a long exit condition ('two distinct complete trivial/no-change reviews since the latest reset' plus case-specific clauses). Pass-report receipts action1 to action6 all show exit_assessment unsatisfied, including pass 6, which was trivial. [M] Passes 2 to 5 each found a new item, so a thorough Luna can keep reporting unsatisfied under a differently worded exit. [M] SPEC S-4 says the model copies printed values and does not assemble them.
findings.proposed_change: Print the exact `"required_trivial_reviews": 0` field and the exact exit_condition sentence as copy-verbatim text. The host appends case-specific clauses after it and never edits it. Add an explicit rule that a finding repaired within this pass does not make the exit unsatisfied. Have the I2 test assert that the copyable sentence is printed. Label 'about 2 passes' as [I].

findings.part: c11 / D7 (script-written Backchain contract, a02) and 'does ShipLoop accept a one-pass child'
findings.claim: ShipLoop accepts any Backchain child today because nothing validates it. The one-pass exit, which completes on a non-trivial report at gate 0, would be refused by every existing ShipLoop terminal validator. The draft's deferral of a02 should record this.
findings.evidence: [M] A grep of skills/shiploop/scripts shows the navigator only prints Backchain resources, the `backchain-check` line and the guidance. No ShipLoop script writes, reads or checks the Backchain start contract or terminal packet. [M] check_terminal in shiploop_test_loop.py and shiploop_quality.py is wired only to the test loops and static-checks. It uses check_loop_packet, which requires 'a trivial report whose exit is satisfied' for a complete packet. [M] _ephemeral_terminal_packet in shiploop_standalone_improve.py requires required_trivial_reviews >= 2 and a trivial last report, and is wired only to Improve. [M] The vendored runtime and its PROVENANCE sha256 values are untouched: ADAPTER.md, until_loop_ephemeral.py and runtime-ephemeral.md match, and contract values are not vendored.
findings.proposed_change: Add one sentence to the carve-out and the D7 text: a future script-written or script-checked Backchain contract (a02) must accept a gate-0 complete packet with a non-trivial last report. It cannot reuse check_loop_packet or _ephemeral_terminal_packet unchanged.

findings.claim: I4 targets the wrong test file, lacks a required change note, and reads the gate from a less reliable source than the exporter already uses.
findings.evidence: [M] The exporter's fixture-driven tests live in skills/shiploop-e2e-audit/harness/test_run_review.py (make_run, and the importlib load of run-review/export.py). test/shiploop-e2e.test.py only exercises run.review_export. [M] scripts/check-release-boundary.py requires a changes/<leaf>/*.md note in the range for any skills/<leaf>/ change, or a No-Change-Note trailer. skills/shiploop-e2e-audit is a skill leaf, and I3 lists notes only for shiploop and backchain. [M] loop_doc in export.py already reads the runtime-written until-loop-receipt.json and shows progress.required_trivial_reviews as 'Trivial streak x of y required'. The draft's source, until-loop-start-input.json, is a host-chosen name; the 1.16.0 run used backchain-until-loop-start.json.
findings.proposed_change: Compare the receipt's progress.required_trivial_reviews with state.md's backchain_passes in loop_doc. Put the fixture cases in test_run_review.py. Add a changes/shiploop-e2e-audit note, or a No-Change-Note trailer with a reason.

findings.claim: A full-text golden for converge mode contradicts the repo's content-pin convention. It would fail on unrelated edits to shared text.
findings.evidence: [M] The BackchainStageTextTests docstring in test/shiploop-navigator-dry-run.test.py says its pins are 'content pins ... not word or byte pins: a packet may grow when an obligation needs it'. The converge text includes shared paragraphs: _backchain_contract_budget (built from loop_contract constants), BACKCHAIN_CHECK and _BACKCHAIN_PLAN_CALL. Any legitimate change to them would break an exact golden. [I] The existing pins already cover the content that matters: the two-consecutive sentence and required_trivial_reviews: 2 in test_native_backchain_operations_reuse_selected_until_loop_subcall, and the obligations list in test_the_loop_stage_keeps_every_obligation_the_trim_did_not_target.
findings.proposed_change: Pin converge mode by content: the two-consecutive sentence, 'required_trivial_reviews: 2', and the unchanged obligation phrases. Pin one mode by 'required_trivial_reviews: 0', the absence of the two-consecutive sentence, and the retained obligations. Drop the whole-text golden.
